cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: The Approved Explanation
cards.instruction: Protect someone or the group by maintaining a simplified account that everyone can safely repeat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Grandad's embarrassed about the gazebo. Let's tell everyone the party moved indoors because the garden's unavailable.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: He's already told Aunt Jean he set it on fire.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then we all say, 'Everyone's fine; we're celebrating indoors.'

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Jean wants him to explain it in his birthday speech.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's his opening sentence too. Then straight to thanking her for the trifle.

mechanism: A takes final control of the shared wording to protect a vulnerable person or group, approving only a simple repeatable account responsive to new facts.
confusable: Personal blame evasion is confusable: the protected person or group must be identified, and the simplified account must not merely shelter A own role.
comparison: School account reduces worry and conflicting versions about a driver; family account protects an embarrassed birthday celebrant from retelling a fire story.
seedUse: Read both cards and all four seeds. Preserve factual updates and protective motive; do not mistake simplified reassurance for proof of unseen facts or historical acceptance.
